races.name: Join Fitzdares For A Personal Service Nursery

runners_data.name: Jaijai
runners_data.note: Won over this exact 5f trip on good going 24 days ago and holds the most natural right to the lead; Richard Hannon's juveniles handle fast ground well, though the style-fit tag (0.90) reminds us this is a prominent rather than true front-running profile, and Joe Leavy must commit early to make the most of a light field.
runners_data.comment: Jaijai won last time out, the peak of a progressive profile that reads sixth then second beforehand, and today's trip and going are proven. Three weeks off is a minor query, but that upward curve gives him strong claims.

runners_data.name: Undercover Affair
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy's booking is the standout angle — six runs have built solid consistency (three placings, one win on soft) and five outings on similar going show 3P from 5, making this trip and surface a known quantity; naturally prominent, the horse will look to sit close to Jaijai and deploy a late kick.
runners_data.comment: Placed in five of his last six starts, sandwiching a win, and quick to post again 11 days on with today's trip and going both familiar to him. He has not added to that success since, though, and needs to find more to regain the front rank.

runners_data.name: Terminology
runners_data.note: James Doyle takes the mount on an Archie Watson two-year-old with just two runs but a 5f win on good already banked; a true prominent type placed at the rear on the pace map purely through redistribution in a light field, so do not read it as a hold-up specialist — it will race close up and its chance is live if pace is honest.
runners_data.comment: Successful last time out having been third two starts back, resurfacing 16 days on with today's trip and going nothing new to her. Those claims are tempered, though, by a yard currently firing few winners — just 3% over the last fortnight.

races.paceDynamic: Jaijai is the confirmed pace-setter here and, with only three runners on a flat Windsor 5f, will stride to the front unchallenged from the off and set a sustainable, controlled tempo. Undercover Affair and Terminology are both naturally prominent types who will track closely rather than mount any serious pressure, meaning the gallop is unlikely to be truly searching on good-to-firm ground. With no genuine hold-up horse in the field and the pace dictated by one horse who can simply roll along at a rhythm of its own choosing, this race shape strongly favours the horse who can lead or race just off the pace and sustain its effort to the line — a front-runner or close tracker who handles fast ground and five furlongs. The field holds more prominent-minded types than can realistically all secure a forward position; Jaijai is best placed to lead, with Undercover Affair and Terminology both needing to slot in behind rather than fulfil their natural front-running preferences.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Jaijai Controls And Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Jaijai leads at a comfortable clip and the modest field fails to apply meaningful pressure at any stage.
scenarios.body: Jaijai rolls along unchallenged on good-to-firm ground, setting a rhythm that plays to its own fitness and recent 5f win, and the two trackers simply cannot find the gear to collar it.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tracker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Undercover Affair tracks Jaijai closely throughout and unleashes a sharp, well-timed challenge inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Oisin Murphy's positional intelligence gives Undercover Affair an ideal stalking position just off Jaijai's shoulder, and with strong recent 5f form on similar going the mare is capable of wearing the leader down close home.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Terminology Outstays Both
scenarios.trigger: If Terminology, despite being a natural prominent type mapped to a tracking role, travels smoothly enough to arrive with a sustained late challenge.
scenarios.body: James Doyle extracts maximum efficiency from a horse with a 5f win already on good ground, and if Jaijai's uncontested lead has been deceptively quick Terminology could benefit from a well-judged run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddled Tactical Affair
scenarios.trigger: If all three jockeys contest the early lead creating a scrappy, contested pace that unsettles the field's rhythm.
scenarios.body: A messy early battle between three prominent types on fast ground could produce an uncharacteristic result, though this is the least likely outcome given the clear pace hierarchy.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Undercover Affair can get to Jaijai's girth turning for home — if Murphy secures that position by the 2f pole, Jaijai's advantage could dissolve rapidly in the final 100 yards.

Terminology's redistribution to a mapped hold-up role is artificial; if James Doyle pushes for early position and creates a three-way scrimmage for the front, the even tempo that suits Jaijai evaporates entirely.
Jaijai's last run was 24 days ago and its form string includes a 6th over 6f — confirm it handles returning to 5f sharply rather than needing a stronger gallop to be seen at its best.

Good-to-firm Windsor 5f is a straight, flat track where early position is critical and leaders are hard to peg back — any horse that gets loose in front here with cover from a small field carries a significant structural advantage.

races.name: Ambrose Loves Reggae EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (Div 1)
Ambrose Loves Reggae EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (Div 2)

runners_data.name: Real Bullet
runners_data.note: Unraced Boughey/Murphy combination on debut — one of the most potent pairings in British racing for juvenile first-timers; style entirely unknown but with Oisin Murphy riding, likely to be placed handy; going poses no concern but the sprint-finish scenario is everything here.

runners_data.name: Rex Regum
runners_data.note: Finished ninth on debut at Goodwood over 6f in good ground — a fade that suggests he didn't handle the pace; Tom Clover sends him back here 51 days later and at Windsor, but the finishing pattern is a concern in a race that may not generate the early tempo he needs to get into it.

runners_data.name: Stoney Wood
runners_data.note: Ran eighth and tenth on his first two starts over 6f, both on good-to-firm equivalent going, so the surface is proven but improvement is required; Stevie Donohoe takes the ride for Michael Bell and the 14-day trainer stat (1/21) is unremarkable — needs more than he has shown to date.

runners_data.name: Bossy Angel
runners_data.note: Rod Millman's filly ran 8th and 9th over 6f in good ground; she is a genuine hold-up performer by nature but is pushed into midfield on the map because there are simply too many hold-up types in this field — her chance is tempered by likely inability to find her preferred rear-end position cleanly.

runners_data.name: Arctic Tsar
runners_data.note: Clive Cox, whose 14-day record (3/21) is solid, sends out this colt who ran eighth on debut at Goodwood over 6f; a true hold-up type by profile placed into midfield by redistribution, meaning the race shape must be strongly his way to deliver — the style-fit discount applies squarely here.

runners_data.name: Bollengo Boy
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's colt ran eighth on debut on good ground at 6f with an unknown style tag — so his natural position in the race is unclear; Rhys Clutterbuck rides and the trainer's 14-day stat (4/33) is respectable; one to watch from the front if he breaks well, otherwise likely in the middle of the pack.

runners_data.name: Coatimundi
runners_data.note: Charles Hills' colt ran last (10th) on debut over 6f at Goodwood in good ground — the worst form figure in the field; Jason Watson takes over and the trainer has a 2/19 14-day strike rate; a genuine closer by profile but redistribution into midfield means he is unlikely to get the ground back he needs, and the form does not encourage confidence.

runners_data.name: He's Readytorumble
runners_data.note: Jack Channon sends out this colt 51 days after a sixth-place debut over 5f at Goodwood; the step up to 6f is an open question but the 5f run showed some pace, and Tom Marquand's booking gives him a professional steer; style unknown, so his position in the race will be revealing in the first furlong.

runners_data.name: Kigali
runners_data.note: Ollie Sangster's colt ran 7th and 6th over 6f, with his best run on good ground, and is ridden by Darragh Keenan; a natural hold-up performer whose redistribution to midfield signals he is unlikely to get as far back as he wants — in a field this compressed, his late finish may arrive a stride too late.

runners_data.name: Market Leader
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's unraced runner is the one other debutant alongside Real Bullet, and James Doyle's booking is a significant pointer from a trainer whose 14-day record is the strongest in the field (7/55 is volume-backed); style unknown means everything depends on how he jumps and settles — if he shows natural speed he could dominate.

runners_data.name: Note To Self
runners_data.note: Gosden-trained colt with the most progressive form profile in the field — ran 7th on soft then improved to 5th over 6f on good ground; Benoit de la Sayette rides and the step onto good-to-firm is the key question; a genuine hold-up type who is correctly placed in his role, making him the most credible of the closers if the pace truly develops.

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in the field and several debutants whose style is genuinely unknown — Real Bullet, Market Leader, Bollengo Boy, and He's Readytorumble all unclassified — this 6f contest at Windsor is likely to lack a dominant pace-setter and develop into a compressed, sprint-finish scenario rather than a true test of stamina. The majority of runners who have raced carry hold-up profiles: Rex Regum, Stoney Wood, Bossy Angel, Arctic Tsar, Coatimundi, Kigali, and Note To Self all show rear-end tendencies in their histories, and several have faded in finishes on similar good-to-firm ground, suggesting this field struggles to sustain early pace. The going report confirms Good To Firm conditions throughout the Windsor card, which will push the tempo towards a sharp, surface-friendly gallop rather than a grind, favouring horses with natural tactical speed. This field holds far more hold-up types than the map can place at the rear — Kigali, Coatimundi, Bossy Angel, and Arctic Tsar are redistributed to midfield, but true pace leadership remains thin. The race shape strongly favours any runner — particularly among the unknowns — with latent speed and the ability to sit prominently and quicken on fast ground, as the genuine closers risk a slow pace that hands the contest to whoever gets the best of the first two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sprint Finish, Speed Wins
scenarios.trigger: If no early leader emerges and the field drifts into a compressed, slow-burn sprint over the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: The unknown stylists — Real Bullet, Market Leader, and He's Readytorumble — will be best placed if they settle mid-division and find a gear late, while the going-to-firm surface rewards those with natural tactical speed over closers who need a genuine test.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Debutant Leads, Controls
scenarios.trigger: If one of the unraced or lightly raced unknown-style runners instinctively breaks quickly and dictates from the front without serious pressure.
scenarios.body: With so few natural front-runners present, any runner that takes up the lead by default — particularly Real Bullet or Market Leader with elite stables behind them — faces minimal opposition for the rail and can control the fractions. On fast going at Windsor, a solo leader who sets a fair but not brutal gallop can dictate fully and repel the field of hold-up types arriving too late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Arrive Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is surprisingly strong and the hold-up horses — Note To Self, Kigali, or Coatimundi — find themselves in genuine striking position despite their redistributed map placement.
scenarios.body: Note To Self, who has shown form at 6f on good ground and is trained by Gosden, is the most credible of the hold-up brigade should the race develop a true gallop that suits late runners. Kigali and Coatimundi are each discounted by their redistribution tags, meaning they are unlikely to secure their natural positions, making this scenario dependent on race shape breaking unusually well for closers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Grind, Attrition
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is modest but the field fans wide and a long, grinding finish stretches out to suit the most robust finisher rather than the quickest.
scenarios.body: Horses who have shown any level of consistency over 6f on good ground — Stoney Wood and Rex Regum — could theoretically benefit from a races of attrition where faders are exposed and the soundest stayer prevails. However, both have fading profiles and have run in last-place finishes, so this scenario remains the least likely of the four given the evidence on hand.

watchPoints.text: Real Bullet and Market Leader are both unraced but carry the strongest jockey-trainer combinations in the race — if either breaks quickly and instinctively leads, they could control the race from front to finish against a field of hold-up types with nowhere near enough pace to go with them.

Kigali, Coatimundi, Bossy Angel, and Arctic Tsar are all genuine hold-up horses redistributed into midfield — watch how quickly they are asked to travel in the first two furlongs, as any of them forced to race outside their comfort zone could burn energy early and fade badly late.

He's Readytorumble and Note To Self are the two runners with the most interesting profiles stepping up to 6f — He's Readytorumble from 5f, Note To Self improving on good ground — and both could prove the key improvers if the race generates enough early gallop to bring them into play.

The Good To Firm going confirmed throughout the Windsor card means the surface will be quick and unforgiving — horses with a fading profile in their form history (Rex Regum, Stoney Wood, Bossy Angel) face a double risk of fast ground compressing the finish even further against them.

With no horse carrying an OR above 120 and the entire field essentially level on official ratings, the race outcome will likely hinge on debut performance from Real Bullet and Market Leader — watch the market moves on both in the minutes before the off as a guide to stable confidence.

races.name: Fitzdares Sprint Series Handicap

runners_data.name: Amazonian Dream
runners_data.note: Form shows a place last time at 6f on good ground, but this mare's genuine hold-up style is compromised today — the field is packed with closers and she is unlikely to find her natural berth at the rear; the STYLE_FIT flag tempers confidence.|
runners_data.comment: A balanced case: runner-up last time out, the pick of a mixed spread that also includes seventh, fifth and third. Quick to return after just 14 days with today's trip and going both proven, though he remains without a win in his last six.

runners_data.name: Tanmawwy
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old whose recent form string includes worrying signs of fading late (flagged ⚠); a natural hold-up runner who will struggle to find space at the back of this big field, and 32 days since last run adds a minor freshness question.|
runners_data.comment: A mixed picture: a solid second three starts back is the standout, but he was pulled up last time out having also finished ninth in between. Today's trip and going are both proven, though he remains without a win in his last five.

runners_data.name: Kiss And Run
runners_data.note: Ran well at 5f on good ground earlier this season but is stepping up to 6f where all her placed efforts have come; a true hold-up type whose tactical position will be dictated by the field rather than her connections' preference.|
runners_data.comment: Kiss And Run was third last time out, and a good second earlier in the campaign points to a fair level, even if a fifth in between shows she is not foolproof. Today's trip and going are proven, and she stays without a win in her last five.

runners_data.name: Hayynah
runners_data.note: A lightly-raced three-year-old with a win and two places from her best efforts at 5-6f on standard and soft; prominent-racing style gives her a natural place in the race shape here and she looks one of the unexposed types worth noting.|
runners_data.comment: Hayynah is hard to fancy on a modest recent sequence of fifth, unplaced and seventh, and although she won earlier in the run, a yard out of form — just one winner from 26 — adds to the doubts. Today's trip and going are proven, but she rates only our eleventh-best.

runners_data.name: An Outlaw's Grace
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon runner carrying 139lbs — the top weight — but holds four placed efforts from five tries on similar going and the 6f Windsor trip matches her best form; Sean Levey booking is positive.|
runners_data.comment: An Outlaw's Grace was third last time out, and a good second earlier in the run underlines his form; today's trip and going are proven. Back on a 16-day turnaround, the one knock is he stays without a win in his last six.

runners_data.name: Papa Cocktail
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer whose form figures at 6f on good ground read 2-5-10-2-2 — an excellent place record but lacks a win in 15 similar-going starts; Michael Herrington yard has been placing horses well (3/17 T14).|
runners_data.comment: A balanced case: runner-up last time out and twice more runner-up earlier in the sequence, with today's trip and going both proven and a 17-day turnaround keeping him fresh. He remains without a win in his last six starts and needs to find those extra lengths.

runners_data.name: Jax Edge
runners_data.note: Two wins from 15 similar-going starts and a recent 6f Windsor win in his history; prominent style suits perfectly here and Ashley Lewis claims 5lb — this combination could prove live at a price.|
runners_data.comment: Jax Edge won earlier in this run but has been in and out around it, only seventh last time out. Today's trip and going are proven and she is quick back after 16 days, though our figures leave her with plenty to find here.

runners_data.name: Slay Queen
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon three-year-old with 44 days since last run and a recent form string of 075-00 that is unencouraging; the longer absence and moderate recent figures make her a harder back even with a hold-up style.|
runners_data.comment: Well held in each of her last two starts, both unplaced, with seventh and fifth the two before that. Today's trip and going are both proven, but a 44-day break and a winless sequence in her last five starts leave her hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Bintola
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter and only true front-runner in the field; won last time out at 6f on good-to-firm and has course experience — STYLE_FIT note reflects the structural mapping, not a concern about her role, which is entirely natural here.|
runners_data.comment: Our selection, and on the strength of a recent win and a good runner-up effort she has strong claims. Today's trip and going are both proven; a fifth last time is a small blot, but she rates our third-best here.

runners_data.name: Media Darling
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand takes the ride on this Stuart Williams four-year-old who has a course-and-distance win on good ground in his last five; 38 days between runs but the form shows he handles this track and trip well enough to be kept onside.|
runners_data.comment: Bottom of our figures here, this filly has been unplaced in each of her last two starts, well held since a win four starts back. Today's trip and going are both proven, but there's little recent evidence to support her claims.

runners_data.name: Sir Alfie
runners_data.note: A three-year-old whose entire recent history reads 8-10-9-8-12 — deeply inconsistent and without a meaningful placing in his last five; Thomas Greatrex rides but there is little in the data to encourage support.|
runners_data.comment: Difficult to enthuse about on bare form — two eighths, two unplaced efforts and a ninth in his last five — yet he rates the leading contender on our figures. Today's trip and going are both proven, but he needs to prove it on the track.

runners_data.name: Under The Twilight
runners_data.note: Harry Davies rides for Michael Blake (0/3 T14); genuinely holds two placed efforts from five 6f good-ground starts and ran 4th twice recently, but as a redistributed hold-up horse he will be racing further forward than ideal, diluting those late finishing efforts.|
runners_data.comment: A leading threat with a fair level of form — a good second three starts back followed by two solid fourths in her last two. Today's trip and going are both proven, though she remains without a win in her last five.

races.paceDynamic: Bintola is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner 6f Windsor handicap and, critically, faces no genuine pace rival capable of pressuring her early — she should stride into an uncontested lead and control tempo from the off on good-to-firm ground. Papa Cocktail, Hayynah, and Jax Edge are the prominent racers most likely to sit just off her heels and shape the mid-race order, while the rest of the field will be strung out in a chase pack. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate — Amazonian Dream, Tanmawwy, Kiss And Run, and Under The Twilight are genuine hold-up horses who have been mapped to midfield because the rear is oversaturated; they are unlikely to find their natural position, reducing their effectiveness and their ability to deliver a true late surge. With a single front-runner setting a comfortable, measured gallop and multiple closers compromised by traffic and positional issues, this race shape strongly favours horses racing prominently just behind the leader — those who can track Bintola through the race and quicken at the right moment will be best placed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bintola Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Bintola leads without pressure and sets a comfortable, true gallop that suits horses racing just off the pace.
scenarios.body: Bintola dictates from the front on good-to-firm Windsor ground, with Papa Cocktail and Jax Edge tracking in a prominent position and being best placed to challenge approaching the final furlong. Hold-up horses are left with too much to do from deep and the pace proves insufficient to bring them into the race.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Override
scenarios.trigger: If Papa Cocktail or Jax Edge press Bintola hard enough to quicken the race and create a true-run sprint finish.
scenarios.body: Bintola is taken on for the lead or challenged early, lifting the tempo and turning the race into a genuine test for the last two furlongs. In this shape, any prominent horse who can sustain their effort under pressure gains an edge over those trying to close from deep.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Escapee
scenarios.trigger: If a well-positioned midfield horse finds a clean passage and picks off a tiring pace pack in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: An Outlaw's Grace or Media Darling — both horses with decent form at the track and distance — threads through from mid-division as the front group ties up, benefiting from a good-to-firm surface that rewards sustained galloping. This scenario only truly opens up if the early pace is faster than expected, pulling the leaders wide and leaving a lane.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Land
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong from the off, stretching the field and enabling true hold-up horses to close.
scenarios.body: Even then, the redistributed closers — Amazonian Dream, Tanmawwy, Under The Twilight — face the structural problem of starting from further back than their natural position, making a winning run from the rear highly unlikely. This scenario has materially lower probability precisely because the horses best suited to it are racing out of their natural role today.

watchPoints.text: Jax Edge has a course win in his recent history, races in a prominent style that perfectly suits this race shape, and gets a 5lb claim from Ashley Lewis — watch for him to track Bintola and mount the most credible challenge.|

Papa Cocktail's relentless place record (four times second at 6f on good-to-firm) suggests he will be thereabouts, but his failure to win in 15 similar-going starts is a persistent concern if the race comes down to a sprint finish.|

Bintola sets the pace from the front but carries a STYLE_FIT flag — if she is taken on earlier than expected by Hayynah or Papa Cocktail, her chance of lasting home diminishes sharply on this flat 6f track.|

The overloaded hold-up group — Amazonian Dream, Tanmawwy, Kiss And Run, Under The Twilight — will be jostling for the same patch of ground in the early stages; any scrimmaging in the first two furlongs could further compromise their finishing positions.|

An Outlaw's Grace is the highest-rated horse in the field on OR (79) and carries top weight at 139lbs; if Sean Levey gets a smooth passage from midfield the class edge could matter in a slowly-run race.|

races.name: Find Us At fitzdares.com Handicap

runners_data.name: Candonomore
runners_data.note: Front-runner with headgear (tp) who posted a win 16 days ago, well-suited to Good to Firm and likely to get a soft lead here, but the style-fit flag suggests he is stretching into a prominent role rather than a pure lead role — his strong suit is front-running and he should be respected as the likely pace-setter.
runners_data.comment: Candonomore won earlier in this run after back-to-back runner-up efforts, though the form has since dipped to sixth and eighth. Back quickly after 16 days with today's trip and going proven, he rates the pick of this field on our figures.

runners_data.name: Cristo
runners_data.note: Won over this exact trip and surface combination recently for Richard Hannon with Sean Levey aboard, sits naturally prominent and has the form to track a soft pace and sustain a challenge; four places from 15 runs in similar going underlines his competence on quick ground.
runners_data.comment: Our selection on the back of a win last time out, backing up quickly on a 10-day turnaround with today's trip and going both proven. The profile before that win was mixed, including an unseated run, but the latest form is what counts.

runners_data.name: Mollie Foster
runners_data.note: Returns after a 111-day absence for Mark Loughnane and most of her form has come on Tapeta rather than turf, making this a harder read on Good to Firm; the prominent style fits the race but the layoff and surface switch introduce genuine uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: A leading threat if she can rediscover the form that saw her win four starts back, though her last three starts have all ended in sixth. Today's trip and going are both proven, but a 111-day absence is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Newfangled
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent racer whose natural position is pressed to the fore, but with Candonomore, Cristo, and others also forward-going, Jonathan Portman's five-year-old is more likely than not to find herself shuffled into midfield — her best form has come when allowed to race up with the pace, so the redistribution is a meaningful cost.
runners_data.comment: One of the weaker runners, this gelding won two starts back but has otherwise been modest, a third last time out and a fifth before that win. Today's trip and going are both proven, and a 49-day break leaves him fresh, but there's little else in his favour.

runners_data.name: Tribal Rhythm
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand takes the ride on this hold-up horse who was second over this exact course and distance in similar going, 76 days off — that Windsor form is the most directly relevant piece of evidence in the race and gives him a clear profile fit for the dominant scenario.
runners_data.comment: A leading threat on the strength of a solid second two starts back, with today's trip and going both proven despite indifferent efforts either side of it. He remains without a win in his last five, and a 76-day absence adds a real question over readiness.

runners_data.name: Bold Impact
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy adds appeal but the trainer has 0 winners from 16 runners in the last 14 days, and Bold Impact's history shows front-rank form that he is unlikely to reproduce here given the pace already ahead of him — his best finishes have come when able to race prominently, which this field shape makes difficult.
runners_data.comment: Bold Impact ran his best recent race when third two runs back, but the rest of his form reads modestly — fourths, a seventh and an unplaced run. Quick back after 14 days with distance and going proven, he stays without a win in his last six.

runners_data.name: Kalokalo
runners_data.note: Three-year-old in good recent form (wins at 8f and 10f, a string of placed efforts), carrying the lightest weight at 131lbs for Charles Hills; naturally a prominent racer but squeezed into midfield by the field composition, his low weight could be decisive if the race turns into a sprint but he is not operating in his preferred position.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out and in the frame in all five recent starts — two wins and three placings — fit again on an 8-day turnaround with today's trip and going both proven. Our rating still has him only mid-pack, some way off this field's pace.

runners_data.name: Knowledge
runners_data.note: Simon & Ed Crisford's three-year-old is a hold-up horse whose last four runs have all been at 10f, so stepping back to a mile on Good to Firm is an unknown quantity — the stable has had no winners from 19 runners in 14 days, but the style profile is the best fit for the likely race shape and Harry Davies holds a live tactical hand from the back.
runners_data.comment: Two eighths in his last two starts leave him hard to fancy, with his only success four starts back. He has today's trip in his favour, but there's no evidence yet that he handles this ground, and our figures rate him bottom of the field.

races.paceDynamic: Candonomore is the sole confirmed front-runner and, on Good to Firm ground at Windsor over a mile, figures to stride into a comfortable lead from the outset without meaningful pressure from any genuine pace rival. Newfangled, Bold Impact, and Kalokalo are all naturally prominent types who want to race close to the pace, but with only one slot at the head of affairs there will be a quiet jostling for position in the first two furlongs — none of the three is likely to get their ideal berth, and at least one will be shuffled back from their natural role. The field contains more forward-travelling horses than the race shape can accommodate, meaning Candonomore should enjoy a controlled, sustainable tempo that neither collapses into a crawl nor genuinely punishes stamina. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with a late turn of foot, and also rewards any prominent runner who manages to settle just off Candonomore's shoulder and cover the move — Cristo, sitting naturally prominent and in excellent recent form, is ideally placed to exploit this if the pace stays honest without becoming searching.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Candonomore Controls, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Candonomore leads at a fair but sustainable gallop and the prominent pack never truly pressures him early, setting up a finish where late runners launch off his back.
scenarios.body: Candonomore dictates from the front at a tempo that looks controlled but leaves enough petrol for hold-up horses to pick off tiring rivals in the final two furlongs; the Good to Firm surface at Windsor rewards those with a clean turn of foot rather than pure stamina grinders. Tribal Rhythm and Knowledge, operating from off the pace, are the profile types who benefit most from this scenario, able to track the field and deliver a challenge in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed prominent types — most likely Newfangled or Cristo — succeeds in sitting a close second and tracks Candonomore throughout, drawing clear of the hold-up pack before they can organise.
scenarios.body: The early scrimmage for position resolves with Cristo or Newfangled slotting directly behind Candonomore, meaning the pace is controlled but not overly slow, and the race becomes a two-horse break from the field turning for home. Horses who need daylight and a sustained gallop to produce their finish are bypassed as the winner is already gone.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Slow Pace, Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Candonomore idles in front and the prominent pack are content to dawdle, collapsing the tempo into a sprint-finish scramble over the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A falsely run mile on Good to Firm ground at Windsor becomes a flat-out dash from the two-furlong pole, nullifying any advantage held by hold-up horses who need time and distance to build momentum. Kalokalo, who has strong form finishing with purpose in tactical races and carries the lowest weight, and Bold Impact, who has hit the frame in flat-pace contests, are the types to capitalise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Surge, Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Candonomore sets a fast early clip that burns him out before the final furlong and the entire field sweeps past late.
scenarios.body: An uncharacteristically hot early gallop — perhaps caused by Newfangled or Bold Impact pushing hard for position — drains Candonomore and stretches the field, leaving a vacuum for the genuine hold-up horses to fill. Knowledge and Tribal Rhythm, who both sit deepest in the field and need horses to come back to them, are the primary beneficiaries of this shape.

watchPoints.text: Tribal Rhythm has won over this course and distance in similar going and is ridden by Tom Marquand — if Candonomore sets a fair but not searching gallop, this horse is positioned perfectly to come from off the pace and hit the line hardest.

The three redistributed prominent types — Newfangled, Bold Impact, and Kalokalo — may all try to push forward in the early stages, creating a brief scramble for position behind Candonomore that could disrupt stride patterns and unsettle horses racing close to the pace.

Mollie Foster's 111-day absence combined with a switch from all-weather to Good to Firm turf is a notable fitness and surface concern; watch for how she settles early as a guide to whether the layoff has left her fresh or ring-rusty.

Knowledge drops back from 10f to 1m for the first time since winning — if the pace is genuinely honest and the field strings out, the hold-up style suits the dominant scenario, but a slow gallop would be the worst outcome for a horse who needs to make ground from the rear.

runners_data.name: Silent City
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's four-year-old has strong recent form over a mile on good ground and steps up to 1m2f, where the extra distance is the main query; strong pace-setting profile suits this flat Windsor track and Dawson keeps things simple, though the OR-82 mark and slightly unfamiliar trip introduce a small doubt.
runners_data.comment: A progressive filly, winning three starts back and placed either side of it, she returns on an 18-day break with today's trip and going both proven. Our rating puts her among the leading contenders, though she must add another win to that placed sequence.

runners_data.name: A Major Payne
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with solid 1m2f handicap form in good conditions, winning and placing repeatedly over this trip; Oisin Murphy's booking is a clear upgrade, the 37-day break is not a concern for a horse with this course profile, and the prominent style means he is ideally placed to exploit a controlled pace.
runners_data.comment: A Major Payne won two starts back, with a runner-up effort just before that and a third last time out. Our figures rate him among the leading players; today's trip and going are proven, though a 37-day layoff is the query.

runners_data.name: Morcar
runners_data.note: Pat Dobbs partners a horse whose last run was a win over this exact trip on good ground, giving Morcar the most directly relevant course-and-distance credentials in the field; a hold-up horse by nature, he needs the pace to be genuine enough to allow his finishing effort to land.
runners_data.comment: A leading threat fresh from a win last time out, backing up quickly on an 11-day turnaround with today's trip and going both proven. The four runs before that were modest — sixth, fifth, unplaced, eighth — so the question is whether that upturn holds.

runners_data.name: Shady Bay
runners_data.note: Tom Ward's five-year-old has winning and placing form at this trip on good ground, and the headgear (tongue tie) is retained; a genuine hold-up horse by style, the redistribution into midfield reflects how many closers are present — he will need to race closer than he'd ideally like, which could compromise his finishing kick.
runners_data.comment: A pair of thirds in her last two starts show a fair level of form, with her only win coming three starts back. Today's trip and going are both proven and a 20-day break leaves her fresh, though there's little to make her stand out.

runners_data.name: Special Ghaiyyath
runners_data.note: The Charalambous & Clutterbuck runner steps back up in trip having run his best recent race over 8f, and the yard's 0/4 14-day record adds caution; racing out of a natural hold-up role into midfield due to the crowded closer's market is an additional practical challenge on what looks an exposed profile at this level.
runners_data.comment: A downward curve reads sixth, eighth and ninth in his last three, though a third four starts back shows there's ability there. Quick to return just 10 days on, with today's trip and going both proven, but he's yet to win in his last five.

runners_data.name: Pomme Pomme
runners_data.note: Jack Channon's four-year-old returns from an 88-day absence which is the most significant concern, though she boasts a course and distance win and placed effort in good conditions; a hold-up runner by profile, apprentice Rose Dawes takes off a useful 5lb but the layoff must be respected.
runners_data.comment: Well held in ninth last time and without another win since scoring five starts back, this filly returns from an 88-day absence rated the outsider. Today's trip and going are proven, and a red-hot yard (26% winners in a fortnight) offers some hope.

runners_data.name: Eupator
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's four-year-old has patchy recent form and the sim-going record (2/15, zero wins) on this type of surface is a notable flag; Sean Levey's experience and the prominent style keep him relevant, but the overall profile suggests he is most dangerous as a place prospect if the race clicks for him rather than a headline performer.
runners_data.comment: A leading threat, back just 10 days after his last run and already proven over today's trip and going, with a solid second three starts back his best effort. Still winless in his last six starts, the obvious knock against a horse we rate highly.

races.paceDynamic: Silent City is the lone confirmed front runner here and, with no genuine challenger willing to push forward, shapes to dictate from the front at a measured, comfortable tempo over this 1m2f trip on good-to-firm ground at Windsor. A Major Payne and Eupator are the prominent types most likely to track in second and third, meaning the race will be strung out in an orderly procession rather than develop into a contested early duel. That controlled pace scenario at Windsor — a flat, galloping track — classically rewards the horse dictating in front or those sitting close enough to pounce in the straight, making prominent and close-tracking profiles the primary beneficiaries. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can absorb at the rear — Shady Bay, Special Ghaiyyath, and Pomme Pomme all want to race from off the pace, but with the tempo likely to be modest, those sitting deepest face the hardest task to close on a leader allowed to coast.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Silent City Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Silent City is allowed to stride clear from the outset and control a comfortable, uncontested tempo.
scenarios.body: Silent City sets a sustainable gallop that never truly tests those behind, reaching the home straight with a length or two in hand and enough left to repel challengers; Eupator or A Major Payne, sitting closest, are the main threats but must break from a rhythm that suits the leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Quicken Clear
scenarios.trigger: If A Major Payne or Eupator improve early to press Silent City and the race develops a proper end-to-end pace.
scenarios.body: With more pressure on Silent City, the tempo rises and the race becomes a test of genuine stamina, which suits A Major Payne's solid 1m2f handicap form in good conditions; Eupator is capable of a bold show on similar going.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer Gets Into It Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is hot enough to string the field out and a hold-up horse produces a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: Morcar's recent Windsor win at this trip and strong course-form record gives him the clearest credentials if the pace fires up enough to allow a late challenge; Shady Bay has winning form at the trip on good ground but is asked to race closer than ideal given the redistribution.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Bunches, Turnover Upset
scenarios.trigger: If pace collapses in the straight and backmarkers benefit from a blanket finish.
scenarios.body: Pomme Pomme — returning from 88 days off but with proven course and distance form — is the most dangerous if chaos unfolds at the death; Special Ghaiyyath would need everything to go right on a trip longer than its comfort zone.

watchPoints.text: Silent City must be monitored for how quickly it establishes the lead — if it is allowed to roll clear uncontested in the first furlong, the race shape locks in immediately in its favour.

Morcar's hold-up style means he needs genuine pace to close into; watch the early splits and if the field dawdles, his chance is significantly compromised regardless of his sharp course-and-distance form.

A Major Payne's response to Oisin Murphy's hands and the step from 1m2f soft to good-to-firm is the key unknown — if Murphy moves forward earlier than expected this horse could change the shape entirely.

Pomme Pomme's 88-day absence makes her opening show critical — if she travels fluently into the race in the first half mile it suggests she is fit; any sign of laboured movement through the early part of the race should be noted before committing to any later assessment.

Shady Bay and Special Ghaiyyath are both true hold-up runners mapped into midfield — watch whether either can actually assert a natural hold-up position at the rear in running, as any improvement in their true tactical deployment would improve their chances in Scenario C.

runners_data.name: Shadow Brigade
runners_data.note: A hold-up type for George Scott and Oisin Murphy stepping up from 7f sprints where recent form reads 7-8-3-7 — the distance step to 1m2f is significant and unproven, and the similar-going record on Good shows 0 wins from 4 attempts; needs others to do the donkey work.|
runners_data.comment: Without a win in his last four starts, though a promising third three starts back hints at more, before finishes of eighth and seventh since. Quick to reappear 11 days on from draw one carrying 135 lb, he needs to rediscover that level of form.

runners_data.name: Impossible Mission
runners_data.note: John Butler's three-year-old has solid form in 12f and 10f company and arrives here 21 days fresh, but the horse is a genuine hold-up type pressed into a midfield role by the shape of this field — its positional freedom is restricted and Ray Dawson will need the pace to truly collapse for a decisive finish to materialise.|
runners_data.comment: Consistently in the frame of late — third last time and three starts back, sandwiching a fourth — a step up on the sixth and seventh further back, with today's trip and going both already negotiated. He heads our figures three weeks on, though still without a win in that sequence.

runners_data.name: Darn Hot Dame
runners_data.note: Tom Ward's filly is the one prominent horse who can travel in Lady Milton's slipstream and exploit any weakening — crucially she has won over 12f on Good ground already this season, and Ashley Lewis's 5lb claim makes the weight attractive; her headgear note flags consistency of intent.|
runners_data.comment: A modest recent record — one win sandwiched by finishes no better than third — leaves her fifth of five on our figures, though today's trip and going are already familiar territory. Freshened by 24 days, there is little in the form to inspire real confidence.

runners_data.name: Bintsaleh
runners_data.note: William Haggas's charge returns after an 80-day break, which is the longest layoff in this field and demands respect as a fitness question, though a 0W1P record in three similar-going runs suggests she finds this conditions competitive; Tom Marquand's riding style suits a patient hold-up horse if the pace obliges.|
runners_data.comment: A creditable third two starts back is the highlight of a modest recent record, with today's trip already under her belt from past experience. An 80-day absence since is the main concern, returning from draw five carrying 134 lb.

runners_data.name: Lady Milton
runners_data.note: Jonathan Portman's filly is unambiguously the race-shaper — five career wins and a 1-2-1-1-1 recent record all came from a front-running or prominent position, and on Good to Firm Windsor ground with only Darn Hot Dame to contest early, she sets the terms; the style_fit tag reminds us that a flat-out pace is not her game, which is precisely why this moderate-gallop shape suits her best.|
runners_data.comment: Three wins in a row form the backbone of a strong recent record, with only a second and a third since to suggest any softening, and today's trip is already familiar to her. A month off since that latest run is the main query.

races.paceDynamic: Lady Milton is the sole confirmed pace-setter in this five-runner field and, with no genuine rival willing to dispute the lead, she should bowl along comfortably at a sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground at Windsor. Darn Hot Dame is the only other horse likely to sit close to the pace, but her prominent style is secondary to Lady Milton's front-running intent, meaning Lady Milton controls both tempo and race shape throughout. The three hold-up types — Shadow Brigade, Impossible Mission and Bintsaleh — will be ranged behind with little choice but to track and wait, though the field contains more genuine hold-up horses than the back positions can fully absorb. In a race where one horse dictates an unhurried, controlled tempo with no pressure, the clear tactical verdict is that prominently-placed horses and those with the tactical flexibility to sit just off a fair pace are most advantaged, while deep closers risk running into a finish already decided by the front end; the field holds more hold-up types than the map places at the rear, with Impossible Mission the most likely to be squeezed out of its natural position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lady Milton Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Lady Milton leads uncontested and dictates a fair-to-moderate tempo throughout the 1m2f.
scenarios.body: Lady Milton holds every card from the front on Good to Firm ground, using Windsor's flat track to set a rhythm that suits her without burning energy — her five wins all came from prominent or lead positions. Darn Hot Dame, slotted just behind, is the chief beneficiary if Lady Milton ties up late, having already won over this course and distance configuration.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Storm Late
scenarios.trigger: If Lady Milton sets a strong enough gallop in the final three furlongs to string the field out and set up a late surge.
scenarios.body: A genuine end-to-end gallop would exhaust Lady Milton and open the race for the hold-up brigade, giving Bintsaleh and Shadow Brigade the ground to close across Windsor's flat run-in.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Darn Hot Dame Takes Advantage
scenarios.trigger: If Lady Milton fades in the closing stages after controlling proceedings and Darn Hot Dame, sitting handy, pounces.
scenarios.body: Darn Hot Dame's hat-a-good-record in similar going and her record of winning over 12f on Good ground makes her the natural heir to a vacating front-runner. Ashley Lewis riding a 5lb claim lightens the burden further and could give her a fractional edge in a tight finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Impossible Mission Delivers
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses and Impossible Mission, despite being out of its natural hold-up role, finds clear daylight late.
scenarios.body: Impossible Mission is a genuine hold-up horse redistributed to midfield on the map and faces a shape that is unlikely to suit — its style_fit score of 0.92 flags meaningful positional compromise. With an undemanding pace set by Lady Milton, a big late run from Impossible Mission is the least likely outcome in this specific race shape.

watchPoints.text: Lady Milton — watch how quickly Rob Hornby crosses to the rail at the start; if she gets an uncontested lead by the first furlong marker, she becomes very difficult to peg back over this flat 1m2f Windsor track.

Bintsaleh — an 80-day absence is the standout fitness concern in this field; watch how she moves in the parade ring and whether Marquand is riding for an immediate win or positioning for a place, as cold horses can be held up more conservatively than usual.

Impossible Mission — a genuine hold-up horse in a field that lacks the pace to truly suit late runners; watch whether Ray Dawson attempts to push forward and compromise its true running style, which would further undermine its chance.

Darn Hot Dame — with her proven 12f Good-ground form, watch whether Ashley Lewis slots her immediately behind Lady Milton from the gate; if she misses that second position to one of the hold-up horses, her chance of benefiting from any late fade diminishes significantly.

Shadow Brigade — the trip extension from 7f to 1m2f is the key unknown; watch whether Oisin Murphy holds him up even deeper than usual to conserve stamina, which could leave him too much to do in what is likely to be a slowly-run finish.|
